 Judgment

(PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD) This appeal is filed by the insurance company under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as' the Act') challenging the judgement and award dated 27.08.2016 passed by the II Addl.
Senior
Civil Judge, Dharwad
(hereinafter referred as 'MACT'), wherein claim petition has been allowed and the liability has been fastened on the insurance company.
2. Brief facts of the case are that on 29.04.2008 at about 9 p.m., the claimant along with other boys playing by the side of the road in Jolad Oni, Kalaghatagi.
At that time the driver of the Tempo bearing registration No.KA-20/2562 came in high speed and rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner, due to the impact, he sustained injuries.
Thereafter, he was shifted to Dr.Bhaskar Rao Hospital, Hubli, wherein he underwent operation.
After recovering from the injury, the claim petition has been filed before MACT, Dharwad under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
On service of notice, NC: 2024:KHC-D:17966 respondents appeared through their counsel.
Respondent Nos. 1 to 3 were placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the allegations made in the claim petition.
On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, trial Court has framed two issues to prove the case.
Claimants have examined two witnesses and produced 19 documents.
Respondents have examined one witness and marked three documents.

On appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, Tribunal has allowed the claim petition granting a compensation of Rs.3,02,775/- with 8% interest and fastened the liability on the insurance company.
Being aggrieved by the same the insurance company has filed this appeal.
3. Sri

.S.S.Joshi, learned counsel appearing for the insurance company has contended that as on the date of the accident, driver of the offending vehicle has holding driving license to drive light motor vehicle, non-transport.
But, he was driving the transport vehicle.

Since insured has violated the National Insurance Co.Ltd vs Basavaraj Urf Shivayya Mathapathi on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178453108/
2 policy conditions, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The tribunal erred in fastening the liability on the insurance company.

He also contended that in the light of the Division Bench Decision of this Court in the case of NC: 2024:KHC-D:17966 Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others Vs. Venkateshan V. and others (MFA No.5896/2018 and connected matters disposed of on 24.08.2020), the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 8% p.a. on the compensation amount appears excessive.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Sri.N.V.Yaji, learned counsel appearing for the claimants has contended that even though, driver of the offending vehicle was having light motor vehicle, non-transport, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MUKUND DEWANGAN Vs. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED1, since the unladen weight of offending vehicle involved in the accident is less than 7500 Kgs., he can drive the transport vehicle.

entities.text: MUKUND DEWANGAN Vs. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability on the insurance company to pay compensation.
5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.

It is not in dispute that the claimant has suffered injuries in road traffic accident that occurred on 29.04.2008 due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tempo bearing registration number (2017) 14 SCC 663 NC: 2024:KHC-D:17966 KA-20/2562.

Even though, driver of offending vehicle was holding light motor vehicle non-transport driving license, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MUKUND DEWANGAN supra has held that, if the unladen weight of vehicle is less than 7500 Kgs,
if the driver is holding light motor vehicle, non-transport can drive the transport vehicle.
6. In the case on hand, unladen weight is less than 7500 Kgs.
Therefore, the driver of the offending vehicle was having valid driving license.
Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability on the insurance company.
There is no error or illegalities in the order passed by the Tribunal.

7. In respect of interest is concerned, in view of the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others supra, rate of interest at 8% p.a. has to be scaled down to 6%
p.a.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER 1) The appeal is allowed in part.
The judgment and award passed by the MACT is modified.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:17966 2) Insurance company is directed to deposit entire compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal with 6% interest from the date of the petition till the deposit of the amount.
Insurance company is directed to deposit the entire amount within 6 weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
3) Amount in deposit is directed to be transferred to the trial Court.
